title: hf sync KB mirror is isolated from ambient dirty meta worktrees
objective: The Weave /review run exposed `hf sync --auto` failing the ledger-to-KB mirror step with `git-kb checkout ... Uncommitted changes exist in workspace` because the broader meta workspace was dirty. That makes a fleet maintenance operation depend on unrelated ambient worktree state. Upgrade the kernel so KB mirror/write-back is isolated, deterministic, and non-destructive: use a dedicated temporary worktree/index, a git-kb non-checkout API, or a staged writer that never requires discarding unrelated user changes. Ledger rollup and health remediation must remain independent from KB mirror failure, with structured per-phase results.
acceptance_criteria: A dirty unrelated meta workspace no longer blocks `hf sync --auto` from updating the ledger rollup and from performing KB mirror work where safe.

The KB mirror path no longer runs a destructive or ambient `git-kb checkout` against the operator's current dirty tree; it uses an isolated worktree/index/API or fails with a typed, actionable per-phase result.
`hf sync --json` or equivalent structured output distinguishes A registration, B KB mirror, and C fleet rollup statuses per repo/member.
If KB mirror is blocked, sync exits/reporting make clear whether rollup succeeded and what remains, without hiding the failure in plain text.
Tests simulate a dirty meta worktree and prove sync either mirrors through isolation or reports only the KB phase blocked while preserving rollup success.
